# No shipped ESP32-S3 binary produces CSI on a bare (display-less) S3 DevKit — two distinct causes; in-repo `release_bins` 4MB binary works

## Summary

On a bare **ESP32-S3-N16R8 DevKit** (no AMOLED, no touch, chip rev **v0.2**), **every downloadable S3 release binary yields `yield=0pps` permanently** — including v0.7.1 with the #985 self-ping active. Two independent causes:

1. **v0.7.x s3-8mb (display-enabled build): SH8601 display probe false-positives on bare boards** → the #893/#906 `MGMT+DATA` filter upgrade is skipped → CSI starves at MGMT-only. The write-only QSPI panel init "succeeds" into the void (`SH8601 panel init OK (368x448)`), while the two probes that *can* detect absence (TCA9554 @0x20 and FT3168 touch, both I2C with readback) correctly fail — but don't influence `display_is_active()`.
2. **v0.6.7-esp32 release asset `esp32-csi-node-s3-4mb.bin` predates the fix**: its boot banner says `Compile time: May 23 2026 11:44:16`, but #906 merged June 2 (`898c536e`). The v0.6.7 tag source has no `csi_collector_enable_data_capture()` call in `main.c`. So the only display-less S3 release binary never contained the #893 fix it was advertised to carry (in the #893/#866/#897 close-out comments).

The **in-repo** `firmware/esp32-csi-node/release_bins/esp32-csi-node-4mb.bin` (refreshed by `786e834d`, built 2026-06-02, banner `v0.7.0`) **works immediately**: `CSI filter upgraded to MGMT+DATA (no display, RuView#893)` prints, and yield goes 0 → 27–30 pps.

This is the S3 re-test that was requested in #866 ("Please re-test on your S3 once #868 lands") and #893 — with the conclusion that the fix is correct but **was never actually shipped for S3**.

## Environment

- Board: bare ESP32-S3-N16R8 DevKit (dual USB-C, CH343P UART bridge), efuse chip rev **v0.2**, boya 16MB flash
- AP: Orange **Livebox** (2.4 GHz, channel 1, WPA2-PSK, phy bgn, BW20), quiet residential RF, RSSI −56…−67
- Host: macOS (Apple Silicon), esptool v5.3.0, `sensing-server` built from `main` (`2a307138`)
- Association/IP/UDP path verified healthy: DHCP lease, OTA HTTP server reachable from LAN (TCP 8032 answers), `<ba-add>` block-ack established with the AP

## Evidence

### A) v0.7.1-esp32 release `esp32-csi-node-s3-8mb.bin` — yield=0pps despite self-ping

Boot (relevant lines):

```
I csi_collector: Promiscuous mode enabled (MGMT-only, RuView#396)
I csi_collector: CSI collection initialized (node_id=1, channel=1)
I csi_collector: self-ping started -> 192.168.1.1 @50Hz (CSI OFDM source, fix #521/#954)
I disp_hal: I2C bus init OK (SDA=15, SCL=14)
W disp_hal: TCA9554 not found at 0x20: ESP_FAIL
W disp_hal: TCA9554 not found — assuming display power is always-on (direct wiring)
I disp_hal: SH8601 panel init OK (368x448)          <-- false positive on bare board
W disp_hal: FT3168 not found (ret=ESP_FAIL, id=0x00)
```

No `CSI filter upgraded to MGMT+DATA` line ever appears (display falsely active ⇒ upgrade skipped). Result over minutes of uptime:

```
I adaptive_ctrl: medium tick: state=8 yield=0pps motion=0.00 presence=0.00 rssi=-62
```

**Controlled traffic test:** 381 HTTP GETs to the node's own OTA endpoint in 20 s (each a full TCP exchange ⇒ guaranteed unicast OFDM HT data frames to the STA, AP had an active BA session) → **yield stayed 0pps for the entire window**. Note this also means the #954 expectation that gateway ping replies "drive the CSI engine regardless of promiscuous filter state" did **not** hold on this board (S3 rev v0.2): 50 Hz self-ping + heavy directed unicast produced **zero** CSI callbacks under MGMT-only. With MGMT+DATA (binary C below) the same traffic produces 27–30 pps, so the practical fix is the filter upgrade — but the #954 claim may deserve a footnote.

### B) v0.6.7-esp32 release asset `esp32-csi-node-s3-4mb.bin` — predates the fix

```
I app_init: App version:      0.6.7
I app_init: Compile time:     May 23 2026 11:44:16   <-- #906 merged 2026-06-02
...
I csi_collector: Promiscuous mode enabled (MGMT-only, RuView#396)
(no MGMT+DATA upgrade line; yield=0pps; 261 HTTP GETs/15s → still 0pps)
```

`git show v0.6.7-esp32:firmware/esp32-csi-node/main/main.c` contains no `enable_data_capture` call — consistent.

### C) In-repo `release_bins/esp32-csi-node-4mb.bin` (786e834d, built 2026-06-02) — works

```
I main: ESP32-S3 CSI Node (ADR-018 / ADR-110) — v0.7.0 — Node ID: 1
I csi_collector: Promiscuous mode enabled (MGMT-only, RuView#396)
I csi_collector: CSI filter upgraded to MGMT+DATA (no display, RuView#893)
I csi_collector: CSI cb #1: len=384 rssi=-61 ch=1
...
I adaptive_ctrl: medium tick: state=5 yield=27pps ...   (3–5 pps ambient, 27–30 pps under traffic)
```

Server side: node registers in `/api/v1/mesh`, `csi_fps_ema ≈ 35`, end-to-end pipeline live.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Refresh the release assets** with post-#906 display-less S3 binaries (both 8 MB and 4 MB) — currently a bare-S3 user following the release page cannot get CSI at all, and the in-repo `release_bins` workaround is hard to discover.
2. **Harden `display_is_active()`**: gate it on the probes that can actually fail on bare hardware (TCA9554 / FT3168 I2C readback — both correctly returned ESP_FAIL here) instead of the write-only SH8601 QSPI init. On this board the existing logs already contain everything needed for a correct decision.
3. Optionally provide an **NVS override** (e.g. `display=0/1` via `provision.py`) so field units can force the filter behavior without reflashing a different variant.

Happy to test candidate binaries on this N16R8 — it reliably reproduces both failure modes.

---
_Filed with Claude Code on behalf of the board owner after a live debugging session; all logs above are from real hardware (no mocks)._

# Done — and what an evening. 🏆

**The bug report is filed: [github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000)** — fittingly, issue number one thousand. It documents both failure modes with your board's logs, the controlled experiments, and the proof that the fix works — plus an offer to test future binaries on your hardware. You went from unboxing an Amazon gadget to contributing the missing evidence in an open-source investigation, in one evening.

**Where everything stands right now:**

- **Your board** is streaming ~35 radio measurements per second to your Mac — presence, motion, and breathing analysis running on the dashboard at **http://localhost:8080/ui/index.html**. Walk around; watch it react.
- **A keep-alive whisperer** runs in the background feeding the board traffic, because tonight's firmware build predates the "self-feeding" feature. If readings go quiet after a reboot of your Mac, that little helper (and the server) just needs restarting — I can do both anytime.
- **Heart-rate numbers will be unreliable** on this build — that fix came a week later. Breathing and presence are solid.

**The one remaining step, for another day (or now, if you're not tired):** build the newest firmware from source with the display feature off — about 30 minutes, mostly waiting on downloads. That gets you the self-feeding trick (no more whisperer), the heart-rate fix, and every current improvement. Alternatively, the maintainer may respond to issue #1000 with fresh binaries and save us the trouble.

For tonight though — stand up, wave at your WiFi, and enjoy. Physics is watching you back. 📡

# Yes — it's genuinely working. Here's what I see, on your exact screen:

I took screenshots of both dashboard views, and the **Sensing tab** is the one that matters. Here's what's on it, right now:

- **"LIVE — ESP32 HARDWARE"** banner in green — the UI confirms it's rendering real measurements from your board, not simulation.
- **Classification: `PRESENT_STILL` at 72% confidence** — translated: *"a person is here, sitting quietly."* That's you, at your desk. This is the system working, correctly, at this very second.
- **Signal Features** (Variance ~69, Motion Band ~100, Breathing Band ~74) — live numbers that wiggle as the radio environment changes. The under-the-hood APIs agree: presence **true**, **1 person** estimated, breathing around **11–12 breaths per minute** — a textbook resting rate for an adult.

**Two things to do on your end:**
1. Click **"Skip tour"** on that welcome popup — it's covering half the screen on a first visit.
2. Stay on the **Sensing** tab (top menu), then stand up and move around — `PRESENT_STILL` should flip to an active state, and the motion numbers should jump. That's the most satisfying "is it real?" test there is.

**What *not* to expect tonight — so the gaps don't confuse you:**
- **The big black "3D rendering unavailable" box:** the skeleton/pose view needs a trained AI model we haven't loaded (that's a whole next adventure — the project publishes pretrained ones). The Sensing tab works without it; the "Live Demo" tab won't show a person yet.
- **Heart rate:** ignore it on tonight's firmware — that's precisely the fix that came one week after the build we're running (and the bug I documented in our GitHub report). Breathing and presence are the trustworthy readings.
- **The "24 Body Regions / 100Hz / 87% / $30" row** on the Dashboard tab is static project marketing, not live data — easy to mistake for frozen readouts.

So to answer you directly: what's "supposed to be here" tonight is exactly what is here — presence detection, motion classification, breathing estimation, one person, live at ~29 frames a second. The pose skeleton and reliable heart rate are the two upgrades still ahead of us (model download + the newer firmware build).

**The misunderstanding: that green blob is not you, and it's not a map of your room.** With a single sensor, the system cannot know *where* you are — locating people in space takes three or more boards (that's the "mesh" upgrade). What you're seeing is a visualization of the radio measurement itself — energy across frequency bands, arranged artistically on a grid. So when you walk around, the blob won't follow you across the floor. What *should* change when you move: the **numbers on the right** (especially Motion Band) and the **classification** flipping from `PRESENT_STILL` to something active.

# Verdict: it IS reacting to you — the numbers prove it. But two things made it *look* frozen.

Here's the recorded timeline, condensed:

| Time | Motion energy | Confidence | What I read from it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23:17:19–17:40 | ~85–180, steady | 0.85–0.87 | You at the desk, classic "person sitting" signature |
| 23:17:41–18:10 | **drops to ~65–110** | **falls to 0.48–0.69**, flickers of `present_moving` | You away from the desk — your influence on the signal *weakened* |
| 23:18:11–18:25 | **bursts to 180–236, 2–3× baseline** | back to 0.85+ | Strong disturbance — you moving close to the sensor / returning |
| 23:18:26 onward | settles ~70–130 | 0.85 | Sitting again |

Three clearly distinct regimes that track your behavior. The sensing is alive. So why did it feel dead?

**Reason 1 — the label is currently not trustworthy.** The text badge ("PRESENT_STILL") comes from a little classifier that the server loaded from the repository — trained in *someone else's room*, and it openly self-reports **41.5% accuracy**. It's basically guessing politely. The *numbers* react; the *word* doesn't. Fixing this properly is exactly what the project's newest feature is for (per-room calibration — you teach it *your* room in a few minutes). That's a lovely next-evening project.

**Reason 2 — geometry.** The board sits on your desk, half a meter from you. From its perspective, you-at-the-desk are a thunderstorm and you-across-the-room are distant weather. Notice your walking made the signal *drop* and turn uncertain — you left its strong zone. The board senses disturbances along the radio path between **itself and your router**; sitting right next to it, you dominate everything.

**Which suggests a fun immediate experiment:** the board no longer needs your Mac — it streams over WiFi. Plug it into **any phone charger** somewhere 2–3 meters away (ideally so that walking through the room means passing between the board and the Livebox), and repeat the walk test. I'd expect the picture to invert: calm baseline when the room is empty of motion, clear bursts when you cross.

One small caveat before you unplug it: its keep-alive feed and provisioning survive the move (it reconnects to WiFi by itself), so just plug it in elsewhere and give it ~20 seconds. Want to try that, and I'll record another timeline?

content.text:
# The empty room just taught us the most important lesson of the night.

The room was supposed to be silent. Instead, the recording shows **wild activity the entire 75 seconds** — values swinging from 67 to 447, and worst of all: **"presence: True, 86% confidence" with nobody in the room.**

Let me be straight with you, including about my own earlier reading: that "pacing rhythm" I saw in your walking test? The empty room shows the same flip-flopping without any human. I was reading patterns into noise — you were right to be skeptical from the start, and your instinct ("I'm really not sure this is properly working") was better than my optimism.

**What's actually happening:** the board currently listens *promiscuously* — it measures radio frames from **everything** on channel 1: your Livebox, the neighbors' routers, every phone in range. Each source has a different distance, power, and signature. Frame to frame, the "measurement" jumps between sources, which looks exactly like variance — and variance is what the analysis interprets as "someone is here, moving." The human signal is in there somewhere, but it's drowned out by this radio crowd. On top of that, my keep-alive whisperer adds its own bursty rhythm.

**The good news — this has a known, designed solution,** and we already hold the keys:

1. **Source filtering:** the firmware accepts a "only listen to *this* radio" setting — we lock it to your Livebox alone (I have its address: `38:b5:c9:68:91:50`). One radio, one distance, one signature: then the only thing left to change the signal *is the room itself* — meaning you.
2. **The newer firmware build** adds the steady self-generated measurement beam (this is exactly why it was invented, I now understand much better).
3. **Per-room calibration** — the project's newest feature: record the empty room as "zero," so presence means *difference from empty*. Tonight's empty-room recording proved precisely why that exists.

**Your call, because it's almost midnight:** Fix #1 takes about five minutes — you'd bring the board back to the Mac's USB for a moment, I re-provision with the filter, you return it to the charger, and we re-run the empty-room test to see if the noise dies. Fixes #2 and #3 are a fresh-energy project for next time. 

Tonight already produced a working data pipeline, a filed bug report (#1000), and a textbook lesson in why empty-room controls matter. Stopping here would be entirely honorable — say "one more round" or "good night" and I'll act accordingly. 🌙

# The verdict, with numbers:

| | You in the room (sitting still) | Room truly empty |
|---|---|---|
| Motion energy (average) | **211** | **161** |
| Motion energy (median) | 168 | 128 |
| Presence verdict | "True, 86%" | "True, 86%" ← *wrong* |

Two honest conclusions come out of this:

**1. Your body is genuinely in the data** — everything runs about 30% hotter when you're in the room. The physics works; a faint, real human signal is there.

**2. But the noise floor is so high that the system can't use it.** The empty room still reads as "occupied, 86% confident" — because the board is listening to every radio source in the neighborhood at once, and that babble looks like motion. A detector that says "someone's here" about an empty room is, today, not a detector.

So the final truth of the night: **infrastructure fully working, raw signal real, interpretation drowning in noise** — with three known fixes, in rising order of effort: lock the board to listen *only* to your Livebox (5 minutes, tonight if you want), the modern firmware build (~30 min, another day), and the empty-room calibration that makes "empty" read as zero (the project's newest feature, a lovely next session).

Given it's nearly midnight: want the 5-minute filter fix now — bring the board back to the Mac's USB cable one more time, I re-provision, you return it to the charger, we re-run the two-minute experiment — or shall we close the lab for tonight on this genuinely solid result?

content.text:
**Yes — a second board would genuinely help, but in a specific way and at the right moment.** Here's the honest picture:

**What a second board fixes:** tonight's deepest problem was that the board has nothing reliable to *measure against* — it eavesdrops on whatever traffic happens to fly by (bursty, rate-shifting, noisy). Two boards change the game: they find each other (yours has been calling for a partner all evening — its sync radio logs `rx#0`, "nobody answering"), synchronize clocks, and beam steady signals *to each other*. That gives you a clean, controlled measuring line between two fixed points in your room — the difference between listening to random street noise and stretching a tripwire. It's also the first step toward actual spatial sensing (with 3+, the system can begin to say *where* things happen, not just *that* they happen).

**What it doesn't fix:** the firmware and calibration gaps apply to every board equally. A second node tonight would just be a second noisy witness.

**So the right order stays:**
1. **Build the modern firmware** (~30 min, next session) — gives every board the steady self-generated measuring beam and the heart-rate fix.
2. **Calibrate the room** — teach the system what "empty" looks like, so presence finally means something.
3. **Then add the second board** — five minutes of flashing now that we know every trick, and it immediately upgrades the physics.

**Tonight's closing status, for the record:** the board is healthy on its charger and can stay there — but I've silenced my noisy keep-alive (it was proven to do more harm than good), so the dashboard will show the sensor as quiet/offline until we do the firmware build. Nothing is broken; the lab is just closed. Everything we learned is saved — including in my notes for next session — and your bug report ([#1000](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000)) is out in the world.

You came in asking to plug in a gadget and ended up running controlled experiments that reproduced this project's entire engineering history first-hand. Genuinely a good night's work. 🌙📡

def load(path):

    for line in open(path):

w_mb, w_lv = load('/tmp/final-walking.log')

name: esp32-setup-state
description: "State of janos's ESP32-S3 RuView setup — what firmware runs, what's pending, key addresses and commands"

Janos (non-technical, curious; in an office building with a Livebox router) set up a bare ESP32-S3-N16R8 DevKit (chip rev v0.2, no display) with RuView on 2026-06-10.

**Current state:** Board runs the in-repo `firmware/esp32-csi-node/release_bins/esp32-csi-node-4mb.bin` (v0.7.0-dev, built 2026-06-02, display-less → MGMT+DATA filter works). Provisioned: SSID Livebox-9150, target 192.168.1.111:5005 (Mac's WiFi IP). Board IP 192.168.1.31, MAC 14:c1:9f:3b:21:60, hostname espressif.home. Livebox 2.4GHz BSSID: 38:b5:c9:68:91:50, channel 1. Board powered from a phone charger across the room (no longer on Mac USB).

**Why not the official release:** no shipped S3 binary works on bare devkits — filed [github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000) (8MB build false-positives the SH8601 display probe; v0.6.7 4MB asset predates the #906 fix).

**Proven by experiment (A/B with controls):** bursty keep-alive traffic (curl loop) feeds CSI but creates rate/AGC noise — motion_band 192±91 with empty-ish room, presence always "True" (meaningless). No traffic → old firmware starves (yield 0, frozen features). Human signal real but faint (+30% motion_band when present).

**Pending next steps:**
1. Install ESP-IDF v5.4 (CI uses `espressif/idf:v5.4`; firmware README badge says v5.2 but newer docs say v5.4) and build firmware from `main` with `CONFIG_DISPLAY_ENABLE=n` → gets #985 self-ping (steady 50Hz CSI source, replaces the noisy curl whisperer) + #987 HR fix.
2. Then ADR-151 per-room calibration (`wifi-densepose-calibration`, CLI `enroll`/`train-room`/`room-watch`) so "empty room" reads as empty.
3. Optional: `--filter-mac 38:b5:c9:68:91:50` provisioning to lock CSI to the Livebox.

**Key commands/paths:** server: `cd v2 && ./target/release/sensing-server --source esp32 --bind-addr 0.0.0.0` (dashboard http://localhost:8080/ui/index.html, Sensing tab). Python venv with esptool+pyserial+nvs-gen: `/tmp/ruview-venv` (tmp — may vanish on reboot; recreate with `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -m venv` + `pip install 'esptool>=5.0' esp-idf-nvs-partition-gen`). Serial: `/dev/cu.usbmodem21101` (board's native USB port; RTS-pulse via pyserial resets it without dropping the port). Provision: `/tmp/ruview-venv/bin/python firmware/esp32-csi-node/provision.py --port <port> --chip esp32s3 ...`. Flash offsets: 0x0 bootloader, 0x8000 partition table, 0xf000 ota_data, 0x20000 app. User has Brave (no Chrome); Rust 1.89 via rustup installed; no Docker.

Janos (non-technical, curious; in an office building with a Livebox router) set up a bare ESP32-S3-N16R8 DevKit (chip rev v0.2, no display) with RuView on 2026-06-10.

**Current state (end of 2026-06-10 session, ~00:15):** Board runs a **custom-built firmware from `main` (2a307138)** with `CONFIG_DISPLAY_ENABLE=n` — built with ESP-IDF v5.4 at `~/esp/esp-idf-v5.4`, build dir `/tmp/ruview-fw-build` (tmp — rebuild if gone). Boot shows all three wins: MGMT+DATA filter upgrade + #985 self-ping (steady ~31pps, no artificial traffic needed) + #987 HR fix. Provisioned: SSID Livebox-9150, target 192.168.1.111:5005 (Mac's WiFi IP), **edge_tier=2 (digest mode — this is the current bottleneck)**. Board IP 192.168.1.31, MAC 14:c1:9f:3b:21:60. Livebox 2.4GHz BSSID: 38:b5:c9:68:91:50, channel 1. Board on a phone charger across the room.

**Final experiments showed:** empty room vs walking are indistinguishable to the legacy server heuristics (motion_band median 78 vs 78), and even a hand waved 30cm from the antenna doesn't move the per-subcarrier amplitudes the server sees (frame deltas ~1.0 flat) — because at edge_tier=2 the board digests on-device and the raw amplitude stream is sparse/summarized. ESP-IDF py3.9 env needed dotted-name dist-info symlinks for `ruamel.yaml`/`ruamel.yaml.clib` (importlib.metadata quirk) — already applied.

**Why not the official release:** no shipped S3 binary works on bare devkits — filed [github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000) (8MB build false-positives the SH8601 display probe; v0.6.7 4MB asset predates the #906 fix).

**Proven by experiment (A/B with controls):** bursty keep-alive traffic (curl loop) feeds CSI but creates rate/AGC noise — motion_band 192±91 with empty-ish room, presence always "True" (meaningless). No traffic → old firmware starves (yield 0, frozen features). Human signal real but faint (+30% motion_band when present).

# Lab closed — final status. 🌙

**Tonight, in one line each:**
- Unboxed a €9 board → flashed it → found *no official firmware works on it* → proved why with controlled experiments → filed [issue #1000](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/issues/1000) → built custom firmware from source that fixes it → ended with a steady, self-sustaining raw data stream from your room into your Mac.

**The honest scoreboard:** the *infrastructure* is now excellent — custom firmware, raw mode, 300+ measurements/second arriving fresh. The *interpretation* still runs on the project's legacy heuristics, which we proved can't tell your walking from an empty room. That's not a defect we missed — it's the exact gap the project's newest feature (per-room calibration, where the system learns *your* room's "empty" and *your* presence) was built to close. Everything is staged for it.

**Next session, fully prepped in my notes:** build the calibration tool, record your room's true empty fingerprint (door closed, you *outside* this time — it's in my notes, forever 😄), enroll yourself, and watch presence detection become real. After that: the second board, and the heartbeat.

The board can live on its charger indefinitely — it's autonomous now. Sleep well; you've earned it twice over. 📡

### 2.7 CLI flow (operator-facing)

```bash
# Stage 1 — environmental fingerprint (ADR-135, existing)
wifi-densepose calibrate --room living-room --duration 60s     # empty room

# Stage 2+3 — guided enrollment (NEW); prompts through 8 anchors, ~4 min
wifi-densepose enroll --room living-room
#   → "Stand still in view of the sensor…"  [✓ anchor accepted: coherence 0.91]
#   → "Sit down…"                            [✗ low SNR, retrying]
#   ...

# Stage 4 — train the specialist bank (NEW); reuses cached HF backbone
wifi-densepose train-room --room living-room \
    --specialists breathing,heartbeat,restlessness,posture,presence,anomaly

# Status / invalidation
wifi-densepose room-status --room living-room
#   baseline: fresh (drift 0.04 < 0.20) · backbone: rf-foundation@1.2.0
#   breathing  ✓ trained 2026-06-09  conf p50 0.88
#   heartbeat  ✓ trained 2026-06-09  conf p50 0.71
#   posture    ✓ 3 prototypes (stand/sit/lie)
#   anomaly    ✓  · presence ✓  · restlessness ✓
```

---

## 3. Consequences

### 3.1 Positive

- **Fidelity through specialisation.** Six small calibrated heads beat one oversized general model on the cross-room/cross-subject frontier that ADR-150 quantified — and each runs in microseconds-to-milliseconds, on-device.
- **Privacy by construction.** Only the room-agnostic backbone is public (HF). The environmental fingerprint and the person-specific heads stay local; no video, no skin, no cloud round-trip. This is the core differentiator vs cameras and the convenience differentiator vs wearables.
- **Minutes, not hours.** Because the backbone carries world knowledge, ~4 minutes of clean anchors calibrates a room. Re-enrollment is incremental.
- **Honest degradation.** The `baseline_hash` invalidation + anomaly veto mean an out-of-calibration room reports `STALE`/flagged rather than confidently wrong — the same honesty principle as the firmware `DEGRADED` flag.
- **Composable & cheap to extend.** A new biological signal = a new small head over the same embedding, not a new model.

### 3.2 Negative / risks

- **Backbone dependency.** Every specialist rides on ADR-150's encoder; its quality and revision compatibility (`backbone_rev`) are a single point of leverage. Mitigation: pin `backbone_rev` in each specialist; distillation cold-start reduces sensitivity.
- **Enrollment burden.** 4 minutes is small but non-zero, and anchor quality depends on the operator following prompts. Mitigation: adaptive re-prompting + quality gates; ship sane defaults so a partial bank (presence+posture) works after just the static anchors.
- **Heartbeat is hard.** Sub-mm chest displacement at HR frequencies is near the ESP32-S3 noise floor; the heartbeat specialist will have lower and more variable confidence than breathing. The confidence-gated runtime surfaces this rather than faking it.
- **Per-room storage proliferation.** A bank per room per person; needs a clear RVF lifecycle (list/prune/export) — handled by `bank.rs` versioning and the `room-status` CLI.

### 3.3 Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Verdict | Reason |
|-------------|---------|--------|
| One large general model for all signals | **Rejected** | The ADR-150 evidence: scale overfits rooms/subjects and collapses cross-domain; also slower, costlier, less private. Directly contradicts invariant (A). |
| Cloud training of per-room models | **Rejected** | Violates invariant (B): would ship raw CSI of a person's home/sleep to a server. Local-first is the privacy promise. Federation (ADR-105) is the *opt-in* path for shared improvement, exchanging gradients/deltas, never raw CSI. |
| Skip the backbone; train each specialist from scratch | **Rejected** | Reintroduces the "hours of data" requirement the user vision explicitly rejects, and loses cross-room priors. |
| Fold this into ADR-135 | **Rejected** | ADR-135 is *room* calibration (no humans). This ADR is *human-anchor* enrollment + model training on top of it. Distinct lifecycles, distinct invalidation; kept as separate bounded contexts. |

```bash
# Stage 2+3 — guided enrollment (NEW); prompts through 8 anchors, ~4 min
wifi-densepose enroll --room living-room
#   → "Stand still in view of the sensor…"  [✓ anchor accepted: coherence 0.91]
#   → "Sit down…"                            [✗ low SNR, retrying]
#   ...

# Stage 4 — train the specialist bank (NEW); reuses cached HF backbone
wifi-densepose train-room --room living-room \
    --specialists breathing,heartbeat,restlessness,posture,presence,anomaly

# Status / invalidation
wifi-densepose room-status --room living-room
#   baseline: fresh (drift 0.04 < 0.20) · backbone: rf-foundation@1.2.0
#   breathing  ✓ trained 2026-06-09  conf p50 0.88
#   heartbeat  ✓ trained 2026-06-09  conf p50 0.71
#   posture    ✓ 3 prototypes (stand/sit/lie)
#   anomaly    ✓  · presence ✓  · restlessness ✓
```

---

## 3. Consequences

### 3.1 Positive

- **Fidelity through specialisation.** Six small calibrated heads beat one oversized general model on the cross-room/cross-subject frontier that ADR-150 quantified — and each runs in microseconds-to-milliseconds, on-device.
- **Privacy by construction.** Only the room-agnostic backbone is public (HF). The environmental fingerprint and the person-specific heads stay local; no video, no skin, no cloud round-trip. This is the core differentiator vs cameras and the convenience differentiator vs wearables.
- **Minutes, not hours.** Because the backbone carries world knowledge, ~4 minutes of clean anchors calibrates a room. Re-enrollment is incremental.
- **Honest degradation.** The `baseline_hash` invalidation + anomaly veto mean an out-of-calibration room reports `STALE`/flagged rather than confidently wrong — the same honesty principle as the firmware `DEGRADED` flag.
- **Composable & cheap to extend.** A new biological signal = a new small head over the same embedding, not a new model.

### 3.2 Negative / risks

- **Backbone dependency.** Every specialist rides on ADR-150's encoder; its quality and revision compatibility (`backbone_rev`) are a single point of leverage. Mitigation: pin `backbone_rev` in each specialist; distillation cold-start reduces sensitivity.
- **Enrollment burden.** 4 minutes is small but non-zero, and anchor quality depends on the operator following prompts. Mitigation: adaptive re-prompting + quality gates; ship sane defaults so a partial bank (presence+posture) works after just the static anchors.
- **Heartbeat is hard.** Sub-mm chest displacement at HR frequencies is near the ESP32-S3 noise floor; the heartbeat specialist will have lower and more variable confidence than breathing. The confidence-gated runtime surfaces this rather than faking it.
- **Per-room storage proliferation.** A bank per room per person; needs a clear RVF lifecycle (list/prune/export) — handled by `bank.rs` versioning and the `room-status` CLI.

### 3.3 Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Verdict | Reason |
|-------------|---------|--------|
| One large general model for all signals | **Rejected** | The ADR-150 evidence: scale overfits rooms/subjects and collapses cross-domain; also slower, costlier, less private. Directly contradicts invariant (A). |
| Cloud training of per-room models | **Rejected** | Violates invariant (B): would ship raw CSI of a person's home/sleep to a server. Local-first is the privacy promise. Federation (ADR-105) is the *opt-in* path for shared improvement, exchanging gradients/deltas, never raw CSI. |
| Skip the backbone; train each specialist from scratch | **Rejected** | Reintroduces the "hours of data" requirement the user vision explicitly rejects, and loses cross-room priors. |
| Fold this into ADR-135 | **Rejected** | ADR-135 is *room* calibration (no humans). This ADR is *human-anchor* enrollment + model training on top of it. Distinct lifecycles, distinct invalidation; kept as separate bounded contexts. |

While the build runs, here's tonight's final act in four scenes — straight from the project's design document:

**Scene 1 — The empty-room fingerprint** (~60 seconds): you leave (*actually* leave 😄), the tool records what your office looks like to radio waves with nobody in it. This becomes the room's "zero."

**Scene 2 — Enrollment** (~4 minutes, you're the star): the tool guides you through a series of poses — stand still, sit, lie down, breathe visibly, move around — and grades each take like a film director ("anchor accepted ✓" / "low quality, retake ✗"). This teaches it what *you* look like in radio.

**Scene 3 — Training** (~seconds): six small specialist detectors get trained on your room + your body: presence, posture, breathing, heartbeat, restlessness, anomaly.

**Scene 4 — The payoff:** live room-watch — presence detection that actually knows the difference between your empty office and you, because it learned *your* specific physics, not someone else's lab.

One logistics note: the calibration tool needs to listen to the board's data stream directly, so the dashboard server will briefly step aside during recording — normal procedure, it comes right back.

Get ready to be enrolled. I'll call places as soon as the build lands. 🎬

content.text:
# It works. Within exactly what it learned — and that's the most honest kind of working.

Reading your log like a story, here's what your room just did:

**The championship question — answered.** Long stretches of `presence=absent` while you were away or across the room: **the empty room finally reads as empty.** Twelve hours ago, "empty" was a permanent 86%-confident lie. Now it's a clean verdict.

**The detection — real and sustained.** Those long unbroken blocks of `presence=present posture=lying` are you, lying near the board, correctly identified for minutes at a stretch. Within them: heart readings of **82–99 bpm** (plausible — that's the trustworthy cluster; the 141–180 flashes are the algorithm chasing harmonics, a documented hard problem, which is why it mostly stays silent with "-" rather than guessing). One clean **breathing=11.8 bpm** — textbook resting rate.

**The honest gap — and it's beautifully logical:** the system only ever says `lying`, never "standing" or "sitting," and it calls you absent when you're upright at your desk. Why? Because **your stand and sit auditions were rejected** (the motion gate — humans sway more upright than lying), so the bank literally never learned what upright-you looks like. The system detects precisely what it was taught, nothing more. It's not broken — it's uneducated in two postures.

**The fix is small and waiting whenever you want it:** re-run the enrollment (it only re-asks what's missing is not true — it redoes all, but it's 4 minutes), with one trick for the wobble problem: *lean against a wall* for "stand still" and *brace into a chair back* for "sit" — borrowed stability passes the 60% motion gate.

It's past 1 AM. My honest recommendation: **bank this.** You went from a padded envelope to a calibrated, personalized, through-wall presence sensor — custom firmware, an upstream bug report, and a trained model of your own room. The missing postures, the dashboard hookup, the second board, the heartbeat polish — all of that keeps. Say the word either way: one more enrollment round, or I write the final notes and we call it a triumph. 🏆

Janos (non-technical, curious; in an office building with a Livebox router) set up a bare ESP32-S3-N16R8 DevKit (chip rev v0.2, no display) with RuView on 2026-06-10.

**Current state (end of 2026-06-10 session, ~00:15):** Board runs a **custom-built firmware from `main` (2a307138)** with `CONFIG_DISPLAY_ENABLE=n` — built with ESP-IDF v5.4 at `~/esp/esp-idf-v5.4`, build dir `/tmp/ruview-fw-build` (tmp — rebuild if gone). Boot shows all three wins: MGMT+DATA filter upgrade + #985 self-ping (steady ~31pps, no artificial traffic needed) + #987 HR fix. Provisioned: SSID Livebox-9150, target 192.168.1.111:5005 (Mac's WiFi IP), **edge_tier=2 (digest mode — this is the current bottleneck)**. Board IP 192.168.1.31, MAC 14:c1:9f:3b:21:60. Livebox 2.4GHz BSSID: 38:b5:c9:68:91:50, channel 1. Board on a phone charger across the room.

😄 No — that's not me! I live here, in this chat window. Your Terminal is a different creature: it only understands commands, so when you typed "hi, its you?" into it, it dutifully searched for a program named `hi,` — and reported, slightly offended, that no such program exists.

What happened there, decoded:

- The `>....` prompt means the Terminal was stuck mid-sentence — an earlier paste or keystroke left a quote open, and it sat waiting for the ending quote (consuming whatever came next as plain text).
- The wall of celebrity names looks like a **clipboard accident** — a Cmd+V landing in the Terminal with something unexpected on your clipboard. The Terminal swallowed it all as that "unfinished sentence."
- Then your "hi, its you?" arrived after the confusion ended, and zsh tried to *execute* your greeting. 

**Nothing harmful happened** — the only things that "ran" were two failed nonsense commands, which is exactly what the `command not found` lines prove. You can safely close that Terminal window entirely; the board doesn't need it, and it's still on its charger quietly measuring your room like we left it.

But I'm curious on your behalf about one thing: where a list of two hundred actors came from on your clipboard at 1:30 in the morning. That's between you and your copy-paste history. 😄

Anything else, or shall the lab stay closed until next time?

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed
- **ESP32 edge heart rate no longer stuck at ~45 BPM / dropping wildly — #987.** The on-device HR estimator (`edge_processing.c`, `0xC5110002`) reported ~45 BPM regardless of true heart rate (Apple-Watch ground truth 87 BPM read as ~45) and swung frame-to-frame. Two root causes: (1) a hardcoded `sample_rate = 10.0f` that became wrong after #985's self-ping raised the CSI callback rate to a variable ~13–19 Hz — BPM scales as `assumed/actual × true`, so 87 read ~45 and the reading swung as CSI yield fluctuated; (2) the zero-crossing estimator locked onto a breathing harmonic (a 0.25 Hz breathing fundamental puts its 3rd harmonic at ~0.74 Hz ≈ 44 BPM inside the HR band). Known limitation: heavy subject motion still degrades the estimate (motion gating is a follow-up).
- **Person count no longer leaks up to 10 in heuristic mode — addresses #894.** `field_bridge::occupancy_or_fallback` returned the eigenvalue-based `FieldModel::estimate_occupancy` count **unbounded** (its internal ceiling is 10), while the sibling estimators on the same single-link data — the perturbation-energy fallback right below it and `score_to_person_count` — both cap at 3 ("1-3 for single ESP32"). On noisy / under-calibrated CSI the eigenvalue count inflated, producing the "10 persons reported when 1 present" symptom (seen when `--model` fails to load and the server runs on heuristics). Bounded the eigenvalue path to the shared `MAX_SINGLE_LINK_OCCUPANCY` (3) so every estimator on one link agrees; genuine higher counts come from the multistatic fusion path, not a single-link covariance estimate.
